content.title: Paul Skenes' Girlfriend Livvy Dunne Reveals Plans for World Baseball Classic
content.text: Livvy Dunne heads to Houston to cheer on Paul Skenes at the WBC.Mar 6, 2026 3:51 PM ESTLivvy Dunne in attendance during the 2025 Home Run Derby at Truist Park. © Brett Davis-Imagn ImagesKey PointsThe USA opens the 2026 World Baseball Classic against Brazil with a star-studded roster.Paul Skenes, Cy Young winner, headlines upcoming pitching matchups.Girlfriend Olivia Dunne will attend. The 2026 World Baseball Classic kicks off on Friday with seven big games. The USA opens its classic campaign with the first game against Brazil at 8 p.m at Daikin Park before moving through a compact fixture of pool opponents.Watch More Manager Mark DeRosa has assembled a star-studded American roster. Aaron Judge leads the lineup while a rotation that includes Logan Webb, Tarik Skubal and Paul Skenes is penciled in for the first four starts of pool play. Webb is scheduled for the opener against Brazil, while Skenes is lined up to start against Mexico on March 9. Skenes’ girlfriend has signaled she will be in Houston. Olivia Dunne took to Instagram stories to reveal her and Skenes’ airport fits before flying off from Arizona. The former LSU gymnast has been a constant sight at the pitchers’ games. USA pitcher Paul Skenes reacts against the San Francisco Giants during a spring training game at Scottsdale Stadium.© Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images The couple got together in 2023 and, since then, has shared a loving, healthy relationship. In a recent TikTok filmed during a recent exhibition game, she captured herself sitting in the stands watching Skenes represent his country. The clip showed her reacting with a playful smile before cutting to footage of the pitcher on the field. She also recently shared a video pranking her boyfriend by placing pasta sticks in her mouth and pretending he broke her bones while popping her back. The moment captured the lighthearted nature of their bond. In the 2025 season with the Pittsburgh Pirates, Paul Skenes made 32 starts and went 10–10 with a 1.97 ERA. He pitched 187.2 innings, struck out 216 batters, and posted a 0.95 WHIP. Opponents hit just .199 against him, helping him win the Cy Young award from the NL.
